text: {"score":3,"justification":"The core numbers match the card (18.0% vs 2.9%, z 2.18, 58% low complexity, 8 documented 99215s with 0 below billed, 6 of 23, 2% documented). The tone is cautious and the next steps are concrete. However, several narrative claims are unsupported or wrong, and the example claims are mostly not the ones the narrative discusses.","problems":["Rash is attributed to C0091748 and C0092017, but the card lists R21 (rash) for those claims only as a code, and the summary presents it as fact. This is probably acceptable. The card gives no diagnosis names, so the labels for R10.9, J06.9 and M54.50 are inferred.","The claim that C0092367 was flagged as bulk-created is not on the card. It cannot be verified from the packet. The note-check percentages (problems 37%, late 7%, bulk created 7%) are also not on the card and are unverifiable. The script flagged 37.","The headline says the notes show signs of templated or inflated notes, which overstates weak signals. The 7% to 13% rates are low, and 'duplicate and repeated-time patterns' are not evidenced.","The comparison figure of 17% for other providers matches the card, but the summary does not say that the 0% rate is on only 8 claims.","The headline leaning is 'inconclusive', yet the rationale says the claims pattern is 'concerning'. The rationale also contradicts itself by saying the elevated share holds across every stratum while stressing low-complexity patients.","The cited example claims, C0090951 and C0090956, are patients with obesity and diabetes, which do not demonstrate the minor-diagnosis argument made in the text. Claims better suited to that argument are cited in the narrative but not in cited_claim_ids.","The next step asks for charts to be compared against the audit trail, but it does not name the missing pieces (time and minutes not recorded for two supported examples)."]}
